exposure: mode of delivery (forceps, vacuum vs spontaneous vaginal delivery)
duration of second stage of labor (>120 minutes vs <30 minutes)
perineal tear (second degree vs no tear)
cohort: The study participants were women at six weeks postpartum after vaginal delivery, recruited from three teaching hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
finding: The prevalence of anal incontinence at six weeks after vaginal delivery was 8.6%, with maternal age, mode of delivery, duration of second stage of labor, and perineal tear identified as significantly associated factors.
mod_finding: Forceps and vacuum deliveries were associated with approximately 5 times higher odds of anal incontinence compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
